name: The Intern Is the CEO
blurb: The young owner goes undercover as an intern to catch whoever is stealing from her company
title: The Intern Is the CEO: Short Drama Script (Episode 1)
description: A free 2.5-minute vertical short drama script for 4 actors. A young owner works as an intern in her own company to catch a thief. Free to film.
h1: The Intern Is the CEO: a 2.5-Minute Short Drama Script, Episode 1
logline: Nora quietly owns the company, but she joins it as an unpaid intern to find out who is draining its accounts. On day three her manager humiliates her in front of the whole office, not knowing she has just found the fake supplier he invented.
setting: An ordinary office, a filing corner and a stairwell. Props: coffee cups on a tray, a box of papers, a paper visitor badge, a second ID badge, two phones, a coat.

roles.name: Nora
roles.note: Early to mid 20s, the owner in disguise; calm, sharp, plays small on purpose.

roles.name: Victor
roles.note: 40s, finance manager; loud, smug, used to being feared. Any gender works with small edits.

roles.name: June
roles.note: 20s, the other intern; seems kind and nervous, hides a secret. Any gender.

roles.name: Owen
roles.note: 30s to 50s, Nora's lawyer, heard on the phone only; dry and loyal. Any gender.

script.action: Desks, phones, a whiteboard of sales targets. NORA, early twenties, in a plain cardigan and a paper visitor badge that says INTERN, carries a tray of coffees.

script.text: ON SCREEN: She owns this company. Nobody here knows.

script.say: Intern. You're forty seconds late with my coffee.
The lift was full, Mr. Hale.
Then take the stairs. Ten floors builds character. You clearly need some.

script.action: A few staff snigger. Nora smiles and sets the cup down. JUNE, the intern at the next desk, slides her a sticky note: DON'T ARGUE WITH HIM.
Nora sorts a box of invoices. She stops on one. Then another. Same supplier, same round amount.

script.say: Bright Harbour Supplies. Every month. Fifty thousand.
Nobody's allowed to open that box. Victor's rule.
Have you ever seen anything Bright Harbour actually delivered?
No. Is that weird?
It's the address. It's a car park.

script.action: Footsteps. Victor is behind them. He takes the invoice out of her hand.

script.say: Who told you to read these?
You asked me to file them. I'm filing them.
Listen, everybody.

script.action: The office goes quiet. Victor holds up her paper badge and tears it in half.

script.say: This one thinks she's an accountant. She's been here three days. She can't even carry coffee.
I carried yours.
Do you know who signs my bonus? The owner. And the owner has never once set foot in this building. So in this building, I am the owner.
Are you sure she's never been here?
Pack your desk. Security walks you out at five.

script.action: He drops the torn badge in her coffee and walks off. June stares at Nora, horrified. Nora does not move.
Nora alone. She takes out a second phone, an expensive one, and dials.

script.say: Miss Nora. Are you still playing intern?
Freeze every payment to Bright Harbour Supplies. Pull ten years of their invoices. And book the board room for nine tomorrow.
All staff?
All staff. Tell them the owner is finally coming in.

script.action: She hangs up. Takes a real ID badge from her pocket. Gold edge. NORA VALE, OWNER. She clips it inside her cardigan, out of sight.
Empty desks. Nora returns to the box and pulls out the Bright Harbour contract. Two signatures at the bottom. The first is Victor's.
She reads the second. Her face falls.

script.say: J. Park.

script.action: Behind her, June stands in the doorway, holding Nora's coat.

script.say: You weren't supposed to find the second page, Nora. I really liked you.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 on a phone at eye level, and drop the camera a little lower on Victor so he looks bigger than he is. Use a real office or a room with two desks and a laptop; daylight from a window is enough for the day scenes, and one desk lamp sells the evening ending. Record the stairwell call close to the phone's microphone or use a cheap clip mic, because stairwells echo. Do three takes of the badge-tearing moment with a spare paper badge each time, and keep the room silent before Victor speaks so the humiliation lands.

ul: Nora never looks hurt for the camera. She absorbs every insult with a small polite smile; the audience should feel the anger she is hiding.
Victor is funny-awful, not a cartoon. He believes he is the smartest person in the room, so he speaks slowly and enjoys the audience of staff.
Pause for a full beat after Nora asks whether the owner has really never been here. That line is the reveal tease; let Victor laugh it off.
June must play the first two scenes as genuinely kind. If she looks suspicious early, the last line will not surprise anyone.
Owen's voice should sound bored and expensive, like this is not the first strange request from Nora.
A common mistake is rushing the gold badge. Hold the close-up long enough for viewers to read the word OWNER.
Move it to a restaurant: the owner works as a new waiter to find out who is skimming the till, and the manager makes her wash dishes in front of the staff.
Swap genders so the young owner is a man and the manager a woman, or make June an older cleaner who has seen everything.
Change the cliffhanger: instead of June, the second signature belongs to Owen, the lawyer Nora just trusted with the whole plan.

faq.q: Can I post this episode on a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0, so you can film it, post it and earn from it. Put "Script: cv.cm" in the caption or the end credits.

faq.q: Who is J. Park, and what happens in episode 2?
faq.a: Episode 1 only tells you that June signed the fake supplier contract with Victor. Whether she was forced, paid or is protecting someone is yours to decide; the board-room meeting at nine is the natural opening for episode 2.

faq.q: Can I shoot it with only three people?
faq.a: Yes. Owen is only a voice on the phone, so anyone off camera can read his lines, or Nora can play the call as a voice message. The office extras can be one or two friends at desks, or none if you frame tightly.
